chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you pray the Maghrib and the morning (Fajr) prayers, say: 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent,' seven times. For whoever says it, leprosy, vitiligo, insanity, and seventy types of afflictions will not befall him.

He (peace be upon him) said: And when you morning and evening, say: 'The praise is for the Lord of the morning, the praise is for the Splitter of the dawn,' twice. 'The praise is for Allah, who removed the night by His power and brought the day by His mercy, and we are in health.'

And recite the Verse of the Chair (Ayat al-Kursi), and the end of Surah Al-Hashr, and ten verses from Surah As-Saffat, and 'Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Honour, from what they describe. And peace be on the Messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

So glorify Allah when you come to evening and when you come to morning. And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth. And at sunset and when you come to midday. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living and gives life to the earth after its death. And thus will you be brought forth.

Holy, Holy, the Lord of the Angels and the Spirit. Your mercy precedes Your anger. There is no god except You. Glory be to You. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me and turn to me. Indeed, You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful.

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no power and no strength except with Allah (a major dhikr)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended morning and evening supplications for protection from afflictions in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* prescribes a structured morning and evening *adhkar* routine, emphasizing the transition from night to day as a moment for divine gratitude and protection. It integrates specific Quranic verses, such as the *Ayat al-Kursi* and the end of *Surah Al-Hashr*, with unique supplications to ward off seventy types of calamities, reflecting the Shia tradition of using daily rituals for spiritual and physical well-being.
